subject: human skin
title: What If You Wore Sunscreen Every Single Day?

scenes.text: What if you wore sunscreen every single day? Your skin would age slower, and someone measured it.
In Nambour, Australia, scientists followed 903 adults under 55 for four and a half years.
Half were told to put on sunscreen every morning. The rest used it as they normally would.
Silicone moulds of the backs of their hands tracked every line and wrinkle.
The daily group showed 24 percent less skin aging than the others.
Another study blamed sunlight for about 80 percent of visible facial aging. Most wrinkles aren't time. They're sunshine.

description:
What if you wore sunscreen every day? In a 4.5-year Australian trial of 903 adults under 55, the daily-sunscreen group showed 24 percent less skin aging (Annals of Internal Medicine, 2013).
Skin aging was measured from silicone impressions of the backs of the hands. A separate 2013 study of 298 women attributed about 80 percent of visible facial aging signs to UV exposure.
